summary: etude-guest on the test image's serial console, as the debug shell's designated init, without the debug-exit port; the scenario is machine/etudeguest_scenario.c, which speaks etude's frames to it one at a time

cases.behavior: etude-guest started from the debug shell answers hello over the serial console within its frame bound, stores the image's /hello and /ish without a transfer and utils' yes with one, runs a pass, answers the same run command again with the same events and refuses its number with other fields, runs an intended failure, stops a cancelled program and leaves no process of it, reads its end again for status, and execs a program in its own place, whose exit the kernel records as the designated init's

inputs.stored: /hello and /ish from the stage, yes in data frames of 72 bytes

execution.cleanup: libetude-case ends the machine and removes its evidence, which it keeps after a failure

steps.does: boot the test image to the debug shell
exec etude-guest at the debug shell, wait for its alive frame and open the session with hello
store /hello and /ish from etude-guest's stage with put and seal, and yes with put, data frames and seal
run hello, send its run command again, and again with another attempt; run ish -c 'exit 3'; run yes, cancel it after its first output and ask status of it
exec ish -c 'exit 5' in etude-guest's place, wait for the kernel's record that hands the shell back and end the machine with QMP's quit

assertions.checks: etude-guest, started at the debug shell, writes its alive frame on the console
hello is answered by ready, which gives the serial frame bound of 255 bytes and the PID that alive gave
the image's /hello is stored from the stage without a transfer, and stored gives the SHA-256 of the host's copy
the image's /ish is stored from the stage without a transfer, and stored gives the SHA-256 of the host's copy
yes, which the image lacks, is sent in data frames and stored with the SHA-256 of the host's copy, checked on Rach2
hello run as an attempt prints Hello from ELF!, exits with status 0, and every process of it is confirmed gone
the pass's stream for descriptor 1 gives the size and SHA-256 of the output that came
the pass's usage gives the processor time and the peak size, each a number or -, each with its method
the same run command sent again is answered by the same events: the same PID and start, output and end
the run's command number sent with another attempt is refused with error conflict
ish -c 'exit 3' exits with status 3, and every process of it is confirmed gone
yes, cancelled while it writes, is running when the cancel arrives, ends as stopped, and every process of it is confirmed gone
status of the cancelled attempt gives it cleaned, and then its exit as stopped, its two streams, its usage and its cleaned again
exec starts ish -c 'exit 5' in etude-guest's own process: started gives etude-guest's PID
the kernel's record that hands the shell back says that the init process, etude-guest's PID, exited with status 5

progress.means: a step of the manifest has ended

native.reason: the case types etude's frames at the console of a fresh boot, whose designated init etude-guest becomes, which a native run cannot
